english.title: Election official fraudulently attempt to put unauthorised paper into ballot box
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a

(A)_[returning officer]_
(B)_[presiding officer]_
(C)_[clerk appointed to assist in taking the poll]_
(D)_[clerk appointed to assist in counting the votes]_
(E)_[clerk appointed to assist in proceedings in connection with the issue or receipt of postal ballot papers]_

at a

(F)_[parliamentary]_
(G)_[local government]_

election at **(..SPECIFY ELECTION LOCATION..), fraudulently attempted to put into a ballot box at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..), a paper other than the ballot paper which you were authorised by law to put in
english.legislation: Contrary to section 65(1)(d) and (g) and (3) of the Representation of the People Act 1983.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a returning officer, presiding officer, clerk appointed to assist in taking the poll, clerk appointed to assist in counting the votes or
clerk appointed to assist in proceedings in connection with the issue or receipt of postal ballot papers
at a parliamentary or local government election
fraudulently attempted to put into a ballot box a paper other than the ballot paper which you were authorised by law to put in

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 6 months months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time Limit for prosecutions:
NoneNote
Note that for offences committed since 12 March 2015, section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 removes the limits on certain fines given by the Magistrates' Courts. Offences that were previously punishable by fines of 'prescribed sums' and that were limited to 'not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale' or 'not exceeding the statutory maximum', are now punishable by a fine of any amount.
